claim: Treasury and the IRS issued final regulations for the section 48D credit as T.D. 10009, published 23 October 2024 and effective 23 December 2024.
evidence: paraphrase: Federal Register Vol. 89 No. 205 (23 Oct 2024), document 2024-23857, 'TD 10009', DATES: effective December 23, 2024

claim: Under the 48D final regulations, if a taxpayer undertakes a significant transaction materially expanding semiconductor capacity in a foreign country of concern within 10 years of placing property in service, it must repay 100 percent of the 48D credits previously allowed.
evidence: paraphrase with partial quote: tax liability increases by "100 percent of the aggregate decrease in credits" that would have resulted had the section 48D credit been zero for prior years, where an applicable transaction occurs within 10 years of placed-in-service date (T.D. 10009, Federal Register 23 Oct 2024, recapture rules under section 50(a)(3))

claim: Under the 48D final regulations, construction can be shown to have begun either by the physical work test or by a 5 percent safe harbor (paying or incurring 5% of the facility's expected basis), subject to a continuity requirement.
evidence: paraphrase: T.D. 10009 beginning-of-construction rules: "Physical Work Test" or "Five Percent Safe Harbor" (5% of reasonably expected basis paid or incurred), with a continuity requirement (Federal Register 23 Oct 2024)

claim: The IRS states the 48D credit is 25% of qualified investment for property placed in service through 31 December 2025 and 35% for qualified property placed in service thereafter.
evidence: "25% of the qualified investment for the taxable year" ... "35% for qualified property placed in service thereafter" (IRS, Advanced manufacturing investment credit page, last updated 27 July 2026)
